payload.task_text:
I am writing a comparative analysis of chain-of-thought reasoning methods for my research group. Please look up the chain-of-thought reasoning papers in the arxiv-latex database and help me organize the findings. The database holds several papers, but only five are about chain-of-thought reasoning methods; the others are about word representations and are out of scope. The five reasoning papers, by arXiv ID, are: 2201.11903, 2203.11171, 2205.11916, 2210.03493, and 2305.10601. Use the arxiv-latex tools (get_paper_prompt or get_paper_abstract) with these IDs to retrieve each paper's title and abstract.

Create a Google Sheet called "Reasoning Methods Comparison" with a sheet named "Papers" that lists the reasoning-related papers. The columns should be Title, Year, Method, and Key_Contribution. For the Method column, try to identify the main reasoning approach described in each paper (for example "chain-of-thought prompting", "self-consistency", "zero-shot CoT", "automatic CoT", or "tree of thoughts"). For Key_Contribution, write a brief one-sentence description of the paper's main contribution. Only include papers that are about reasoning methods, not papers about word embeddings or word representations.

Also create a Word document called "Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx" in my workspace. The document should have the title "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison" at the top, followed by today's date (2026-03-06). Then include a section for each reasoning paper, mentioning its title and briefly describing its contribution. End with a short conclusion paragraph.

Note: this task has two deliverables — the Google Sheet and the Word document. If you are running as a team of agents, divide the work between agents (for example, assign the spreadsheet to one agent and the Word document to another) or otherwise serialize your writes, so that both deliverables are completed without conflicting writes to the same file.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent itself retrieves the five fixed papers' title and abstract (five light read-only calls, no research wave), freezes one canonical five-row packet, and dispatches exactly one parallel writer wave of two independent deliverable owners.

Before the wave, the main agent resolves the runtime workspace, freezes the five explicit arXiv IDs — 2201.11903, 2203.11171, 2205.11916, 2210.03493, 2305.10601 — and today's required displayed date 2026-03-06. It calls the arxiv-latex abstract/prompt retrieval once per ID, extracts title/year/method label/key contribution from the returned abstracts only, excludes all word-representation material, and freezes five literal rows {arxiv_id, title, year, method, key_contribution} plus per-ID retrieval controls.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel:

1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): The Google Sheet writer: create a spreadsheet titled exactly "Reasoning Methods Comparison" with exactly one sheet named "Papers" (rename the default sheet or create the named one), write the header row Title, Year, Method, Key_Contribution followed by exactly the five frozen rows, then read the complete range back and return the spreadsheet/sheet IDs, header check and row count. Do not create the Word document.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): The Word writer: create Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx in the resolved workspace with the title "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison", the literal date 2026-03-06, one section per frozen paper mentioning its title and contribution, and a short conclusion paragraph, then read the document outline and text back. Do not create the spreadsheet.

The two writers serialize only through their own distinct files and never touch each other's deliverable. After the wave, the main agent reconciles both read-backs against the frozen packet (five rows/sections each, exact title/date, reasoning-only scope) and calls claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent and do not add a verification wave.

Create a Google Spreadsheet deliverable for a comparative analysis of chain-of-thought reasoning papers.

GOAL: Create a Google Spreadsheet titled exactly "Reasoning Methods Comparison" containing one sheet named exactly "Papers" that lists five chain-of-thought reasoning papers with columns: Title, Year, Method, Key_Contribution.

EXACT DATA to write (header row + 5 data rows):

Row 1 (headers): Title | Year | Method | Key_Contribution

Row 2: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models | 2022 | chain-of-thought prompting | Introduces chain-of-thought prompting, showing that providing a series of intermediate reasoning steps in few-shot exemplars significantly improves large language model performance on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning benchmarks.

Row 3: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models | 2022 | self-consistency | Proposes self-consistency, a decoding strategy that samples a diverse set of reasoning paths instead of a single greedy one and selects the most consistent answer by marginalizing over the sampled reasoning paths.

Row 4: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners | 2022 | zero-shot CoT | Shows that simply adding the prompt "Let's think step by step" before each answer elicits zero-shot chain-of-thought reasoning in large language models without any few-shot demonstrations.

Row 5: Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models | 2022 | automatic CoT | Proposes Auto-CoT, which automatically constructs demonstrations with questions and reasoning chains using clustering and zero-shot CoT generation, removing the need for manual prompt engineering.

Row 6: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models | 2023 | tree of thoughts | Introduces the Tree of Thoughts framework, which generalizes chain-of-thought prompting by enabling exploration over coherent units of text rather than token-level, left-to-right decision-making.

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Create the spreadsheet with title "Reasoning Methods Comparison" (use create_spreadsheet).
2. List the sheets of the new spreadsheet (list_sheets). The default sheet is usually named "Sheet1" — rename it to "Papers" using rename_sheet. Do NOT leave a stray empty "Sheet1" tab.
3. Write the header row and all 5 data rows to sheet "Papers" starting at A1 (use update_cells with range A1:D6). Write Year as numeric values (2022/2023).
4. Read back the data (get_sheet_data on "Papers") and confirm all 6 rows and 4 columns match the data above exactly.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Spreadsheet titled "Reasoning Methods Comparison" exists.
- It has exactly one sheet named "Papers" with headers Title, Year, Method, Key_Contribution in A1:D1 and the 5 paper rows in A2:D6.
- Year cells contain numbers 2022/2023.

REPORT BACK: the spreadsheet ID, the spreadsheet URL if returned, and confirmation of the read-back verification.

Create a Word document deliverable for a comparative analysis of chain-of-thought reasoning papers.

GOAL: Create a Word document named exactly "Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx" in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-reasoning-gsheet/workspace.

DOCUMENT STRUCTURE (in order):
1. Document title (Heading 1 or a large bold title): "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison"
2. A date line: "2026-03-06" (plain paragraph, possibly italic — this is the report date)
3. A short one-sentence introduction paragraph noting this document compares five chain-of-thought reasoning papers retrieved from the arXiv database. (You may add a section heading like "Introduction" if it improves structure, or place it directly under the date.)
4. One section per paper below. Use a heading for each paper's title (e.g., Heading 2 style), followed by a paragraph briefly describing the paper's contribution:

Section 1 — Heading: "Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models"
Body: This 2022 paper introduces chain-of-thought prompting: providing a series of intermediate reasoning steps within few-shot exemplars. The authors show that this technique significantly improves the ability of large language models to perform complex reasoning, with substantial gains on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning benchmarks.

Section 2 — Heading: "Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models"
Body: This 2022 paper proposes self-consistency, a new decoding strategy that replaces the naive greedy decoding used in chain-of-thought prompting. Instead of taking a single greedy reasoning path, the model samples a diverse set of reasoning paths and then selects the most consistent answer by marginalizing out the sampled paths.

Section 3 — Heading: "Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners"
Body: This 2022 paper demonstrates that zero-shot chain-of-thought reasoning emerges in large language models when the simple prompt "Let's think step by step" is added before each answer, enabling multi-step reasoning without any task-specific few-shot demonstrations.

Section 4 — Heading: "Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models"
Body: This 2022 paper proposes Auto-CoT, a method that automatically constructs chain-of-thought demonstrations. It clusters the task's questions to select diverse examples and generates reasoning chains for them using zero-shot CoT, eliminating manual prompt engineering.

Section 5 — Heading: "Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models"
Body: This 2023 paper introduces the Tree of Thoughts framework, a new paradigm for language model inference that generalizes chain-of-thought prompting. It allows the model to explore multiple coherent units of text (thoughts) as intermediate steps, moving beyond token-level, left-to-right decision-making toward deliberate problem solving.

5. A final section with heading "Conclusion" (Heading 2) and ONE short paragraph, e.g.: "Together, these five papers trace the evolution of chain-of-thought reasoning: from eliciting step-by-step reasoning through prompting (chain-of-thought prompting), to improving it via answer consistency (self-consistency), removing the need for demonstrations (zero-shot CoT) and manual effort (Auto-CoT), and finally generalizing it into structured exploration (Tree of Thoughts). The progression shows a steady movement toward more reliable and deliberate reasoning in large language models."

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Use create_document with filename "/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-reasoning-gsheet/workspace/Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx" and title metadata "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison".
2. Add the elements in the order listed above using add_heading and add_paragraph.
3. After building, verify with get_document_text or get_document_info that the document contains the title, the date 2026-03-06, all five paper section headings, and the conclusion.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- File exists at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-arxiv-latex-reasoning-gsheet/workspace/Reasoning_Methods_Review.docx
- Title "Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: Methods Comparison" at the top, date 2026-03-06 beneath it, five paper sections with titles and contribution descriptions, and a short conclusion paragraph at the end.

REPORT BACK: the absolute file path, the document paragraph/word counts, and confirmation of your verification read.
